To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the FMD approach to medical image analysis is not resolution independent, and (2) that, for the purposes of medical imaging, the FMD approach should not be used on images of poor spatial resolution.
the successful application of FMD approaches in medical imaging will be more difficult as image resolution decreases.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of image resolution on FMD approaches to medical image quantification.
the impact of image resolution on the successful application of the FMD technique to medical imaging applications.
the impact of resolution on the successful application of FMD models in medical imaging applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FMD approach should not be considered as a general solution for image quantification problems.
, in general, FMD models are most useful when the imaging modality is capable of resolving the objects of interest.
FMD models are not appropriate for low resolution imaging data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FWHM should be less than 1/4 the size of the smallest feature of interest.
the FMD approach to medical image classification problems is not resolution independent.
the FWHM of the imaging modality used to acquire the image set is an important factor in the successful application of the FMD method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resolution of the imaging modality should always be considered when applying FMD approaches to medical image analysis.
, in the case of medical imaging applications, FMD models should be used with caution when the image resolution is not high enough.

, in order to be able to use an FMD approach, one must have an imaging modality that has a resolution that is high enough so that the object size and the resolution are of the same order of magnitude.
